defaultRequirement: Sync products (create, read, update) and read recent orders from a client's Shopify store.
summary: Products and orders are well supported. The real decision is app architecture: who owns the store decides how the app is created, how tokens are issued, and how long they last. Old orders and customer data need extra permissions.

capabilities.label: Read orders
capabilities.conditions: read_orders covers roughly the last 60 days. Older orders need read_all_orders, which public apps must request and have approved. Orders contain customer details, so apps must also meet Shopify's protected customer data requirements.

evidence.title: Access scopes: read_all_orders (60-day rule — re-check before quoting)

clarifications.question: Who owns the Shopify store(s) the connector will use?
clarifications.why: Since January 1, 2026, new custom apps can no longer be created inside the Shopify admin. The right app type and token flow depend on who owns the store.

options.label: Stores in my own Shopify organization

effects.conditions: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard and use the client credentials grant. Tokens last about 24 hours. Read 'expires_in' and request a new token before it expires.

Create the app in the Dev Dashboard with custom distribution. The merchant installs it through an install link (OAuth authorization code flow). The client credentials grant only works for stores in the same organization as the app.

Public app with OAuth. Public apps must use expiring offline tokens (60-minute access token + 90-day refresh token): required for new public apps since April 1, 2026, and for all public apps by January 1, 2027. App Store listing requires Shopify review.

auth.recommended: Depends on store ownership (answer the question above)
auth.why: Shopify now issues tokens differently for same-organization stores (client credentials), client stores (custom distribution + OAuth), and public apps (OAuth + expiring offline tokens).
alternatives: Existing legacy admin-created custom apps keep working, but you cannot create new ones.
Use the GraphQL Admin API. New public apps must use GraphQL rather than the legacy REST Admin API.

blockers.title: "Develop apps" in the store admin no longer creates new apps
blockers.detail: Older tutorials tell you to create a custom app in the store admin and copy an Admin API token. That path is closed for new apps since January 1, 2026.
blockers.resolution: Create the app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard or with Shopify CLI.

blockers.title: Access to the client's store
blockers.detail: To install and test on the client's store you need the merchant to install your app, or collaborator access.
blockers.handoff: Hi! To build {requirement}, please install our app using this link: <INSTALL_LINK>. It requests read_products, write_products and read_orders. Nothing else changes in your store.

blockers.title: Orders older than ~60 days need read_all_orders approval
blockers.detail: Public apps must request this scope and explain why.
blockers.resolution: Confirm whether the client actually needs historical orders. If yes, request the scope early.

blockers.title: Protected customer data review
blockers.detail: Orders include customer names, emails and addresses. Apps must declare and justify the data they use.
blockers.resolution: Request only fields you need and complete the protected customer data form in the Partner/Dev Dashboard.

alternatives.option: Read recent orders and subscribe to orders/create webhooks going forward

engineering.assumptions: GraphQL Admin API, products + recent orders, one dev store for testing.

waiting.notes: Own store: none. Client install: depends on merchant. Public app review and read_all_orders / protected data approval: unknown, often weeks.

uncertainty: App architecture depends on store ownership
Whether historical orders are really required

tasks.title: Create a Shopify Partner / Dev Dashboard account and a dev store
tasks.detail: Dev stores are free and let you test safely.
tasks.doneWhen: You can log in to the Dev Dashboard and see a dev store.

tasks.title: Pick the app type
tasks.detail: Use the answer to 'Who owns the Shopify store(s)?'.
tasks.doneWhen: App type and token flow written down.

tasks.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
tasks.detail: Set scopes read_products, write_products, read_orders. Add redirect URLs if using OAuth.
tasks.doneWhen: You have a client ID and client secret.

tasks.title: Implement token handling
tasks.detail: Client credentials: request a token and refresh before 'expires_in'. OAuth: exchange code, store token; for public apps store the refresh token and refresh hourly.
tasks.doneWhen: Connector survives token expiry without manual steps.

tasks.title: Implement product sync with GraphQL
tasks.detail: Use cursor pagination and respect the cost-based rate limit.
tasks.doneWhen: Products created, read and updated on the dev store.

tasks.title: Test the order window
tasks.detail: Query an order older than 60 days with read_orders only. Record what happens.
tasks.doneWhen: Result recorded in the Evidence tab.

tasks.title: Complete protected customer data and scope requests
tasks.detail: Only for public apps or apps using customer data.
tasks.doneWhen: Requests submitted; tracked as 'Waiting for external party'.
